title: Restart Bluetooth agent when BlueZ is replaced
head: 46b62ae36530
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Existing active bt-agent units are not switched to the supervisor by an update
leads.consequence: On an existing installation with bt-agent.service already active, installing the new vendor file (or reloading units) does not replace the old running /usr/bin/bt-agent process. Omarchy's update flow installs packages and runs migrations but this PR adds no migration to restart an active user unit. Replacing bluetoothd during that same session can still leave pairing without a registered agent until the service is actually restarted or the session ends. Restart only an already-active unit after updating the package, without enabling intentionally disabled units.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F4); corroborated; published

leads.summary: No BlueZ owner turns the enabled user service into a permanent silent poller
leads.consequence: On a machine with /sys/class/bluetooth present but bluetooth.service disabled, missing or indefinitely down, the previous ExecCondition could skip; the new Type=simple supervisor never exits the initial loop, starts no agent, and looks active. busctl errors are suppressed; with the default interval it probes every two seconds indefinitely, including in a lingering user manager after the graphical target stops. The isolated stubbed system-bus error case made 12 probes in 0.6s at a 0.05s test interval and no agent started. The condition directory does not establish that an adapter or daemon is usable. Consider a bounded wait or an explicit daemon/service guard if no BlueZ will start.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1 no-BlueZ case); corroborated; published

leads.summary: A present BlueZ name can lack a busctl PID and be mistaken for absent
leads.consequence: systemd's busctl lists acquired names even if sd_bus_creds_get_pid fails, emitting '-' in the PID column. When BlueZ has a name but its PID credential cannot be obtained, startup waits forever and no agent registers. If that occurs transiently after registration, an unchanged daemon is treated as replaced and its agent killed. Do not equate a missing PID credential with no org.bluez owner; compare the D-Bus unique owner or handle unavailable credentials explicitly. This is a producer-supported conditional failure, not a claim that normal BlueZ permanently lacks PID credentials.
leads.triage: overlaps Opus F2; '-' startup stall kept as conditional, stub-only; published within F2

leads.summary: #12897 replaces the very agent the supervisor starts
leads.consequence: Open #12897 swaps bluez-tools bt-agent for omarchy-bluetooth-agent to handle Just Works authorization. Both heads are divergent, and a three-way merge of their service files contains a conflict. Keeping this PR's ExecStart ignores #12897's pairing fix; choosing #12897's ExecStart bypasses this PR's BlueZ owner supervision, and this PR's systemd-test.sh:10 fails because it insists on the supervisor. Rebase and adapt the supervisor to the chosen agent before either lands together. #12897's reported GitHub mergeable state is MERGEABLE against its own base, not proof of compatibility with this head.
leads.triage: factual; verified pr-12897 head unit ExecStart=/usr/bin/omarchy-bluetooth-agent and live head 87c21cf5; published in related PRs note

leads.summary: #8929's stdin and pairing-window fix is not composed with the new supervisor
leads.consequence: Open #8929 feeds yes to bt-agent and closes the adapter's Pairable window. Its service uses ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'yes | /usr/bin/bt-agent ...' plus ExecStartPost. This PR directly invokes bt-agent and has no equivalent stdin supply or pairing-window close. The divergent unit merge produces conflict markers; taking the supervisor branch drops #8929's actual Just Works fix, while taking #8929's branch drops owner monitoring. If both changes are desired, integrate the stdin policy and pairing window with the supervisor, preserving the other PR's intent and tests.
leads.triage: factual; verified #8929 ExecStart 'yes | bt-agent' at b0e0e257; published in related PRs note

leads.summary: Two other divergent PRs solve the same login-race unit with incompatible ExecStart and tests
leads.consequence: #13258 uses a long-lived shell waiting for bluetooth.service with Restart=on-failure and tests that require that ExecStart; #9131 uses bounded ExecStartPre, StartLimitBurst=3 and tests that require those entries. Both are divergent from this PR. Merging #13258's unit drops owner monitoring; keeping this PR's unit fails #13258's explicit unit tests. Applying #9131's pre-start wait on top duplicates the supervisor's own unbounded wait, and keeping this PR's Restart=always fails #9131's Restart=on-failure assertion. The three-way merged unit has markers at pr-13258-merge.service:5,20,34 and pr-9131-merge.service:12; coordinate/supersede the alternatives rather than merging tests unchanged.
leads.triage: factual; verified #13258 (3549e466) and #9131 (16ce47ec) units; published in related PRs note

leads.summary: The retained NoInputNoOutput auto-accept premise is false for Just Works authorization
leads.consequence: At the Arch-pinned bluez-tools commit, -c NoInputNoOutput registers a capability but RequestAuthorization asks for yes on stdin in interactive mode. Systemd's default StandardInput=null gives EOF; the request returns org.bluez.Error.Rejected. The PR restores registration after BlueZ replacement but cannot make affected BLE keyboards/Just Works devices bond, even when bluetoothd logs no missing-agent warning. This auto-accept comment predates this PR; it is a contradicted dependency premise carried forward, not an introduced regression. #8929/#12897 propose distinct fixes.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing bt-agent stdin/RequestAuthorization behaviour, unchanged by this PR

leads.summary: The stated closed pairing window is not established by the panel
leads.consequence: BlueZ 5.87's default-agent registration calls set_io_cap, which can set MGMT_SETTING_BONDABLE when its default AlwaysPairable option is false. The existing panel only toggles Discovering, and no shipped panel/Bluetooth-device code sets Pairable off on close. Consequently the PR's retained safety assertion that the adapter is pairable only while the panel scans is not supported. This is an inherited unit-comment premise, not evidence that this PR alone accepts unwanted Just Works pairs: the currently shipped bt-agent rejects RequestAuthorization as in H7. It becomes security-relevant if adding auto-accept from #8929/#12897 without the intended window.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing unit comment premise, unchanged by this PR

leads.summary: The new busctl fixture cannot detect losing the org.bluez name filter
leads.consequence: Both test sequences print only one bus name, org.bluez, so changing the new supervisor's awk selection from '$1 == "org.bluez" { print $2; exit }' to '{ print $2; exit }' leaves both cases green. Actual busctl lists other names and sorts by name, so the mutant could watch an unrelated PID and miss BlueZ replacement or hang on '-'. An assertion with another name before org.bluez, including its own changing PID, would catch this plausible parser regression. Run receipt shows both assertions passing against exactly that one-line mutant.
leads.triage: factual; verified from mock source, confirmed by Opus draft-check runs; published as optional test improvement

limits: No host buses, adapters, services or real accounts were queried. Unit restarts, login/logout, hardware pairing and crash cleanup were not exercised; only stubbed busctl/bt-agent were run through review.py.

A direct cross-PR integrated test cannot run before resolving conflicting ExecStart hunks. Merge receipts are source-based git merge-file outputs from each other PR's own merge base, not GitHub's eventual merge resolution.

Related open-PR topic searches include many unrelated Bluetooth/UI/systemd PRs. The diffs of the directly overlapping unit PRs and first-run/unit consumers were read; broad unrelated search matches were classified by file lists, not all individually downloaded.

flags.claim: a transient probe failure causes an unnecessary restart with no agent registered for about 3 seconds
flags.why: The ~3 s figure includes the 2 s detection poll that applies to a real replacement. After a false-positive exit the restarted supervisor probes before sleeping (supervisor lines 18-26), sees the unchanged owner at once and starts bt-agent, so the gap is about RestartSec=1 plus ~10 ms.

flags.claim: these change the same bt-agent.service ExecStart and would conflict with this one (list includes #9131)
flags.why: #9131 at 16ce47ec keeps ExecStart=/usr/bin/bt-agent -c NoInputNoOutput; it replaces ExecCondition with an ExecStartPre wait and adds StartLimitIntervalSec=120/StartLimitBurst=3. The conflict claim itself holds for all four listed PRs.

flags.claim: Whichever agent lands, the owner supervision here would need to wrap it.
flags.why: #12897's agent already re-registers when org.bluez reappears: it calls RegisterAgent and RequestDefaultAgent from the name-appeared callback of Gio.bus_watch_name_on_connection(BUS, "org.bluez", ...). Source reading only, not run. The supervision is still relevant for the bt-agent-based variants (#13258, #9131, #8929).

flags.claim: probe only the org.bluez owner ..., which also resolves the second finding below
flags.why: The owner probe removes the PID-column '-' case, but the reproduced case (s8) was a failed busctl call, and a GetNameOwner probe can fail the same way; the second finding's error handling is still needed. Line 46 states this correctly.

flags.claim: a small but permanent background cost on every Omarchy session
flags.why: The unit only runs where /sys/class/bluetooth exists (ConditionPathIsDirectory, unit line 4) and bt-agent.service is enabled; machines without the bluetooth class directory (for example many VMs) skip it.

flags.claim: add a migration that restarts the unit only if it is already running, for example systemctl --user try-restart bt-agent.service
flags.why: Dropped part of my suggestion. try-restart leaves inactive units alone, so the sessions named in line 50, whose unit was skipped by the old ExecCondition, stay inactive. My report proposed try-restart or restart-if-enabled.

flags.claim: lists every unique, well-known and activatable name and queries credentials for each one
flags.why: Activatable-only names are printed without a credentials query; credentials are queried for every owned name. In the measured bus every listed name was owned (124 GetConnectionCredentials for 124 names), so the numbers stand. My report had the same overstatement.

flags.claim: would fail on a behaviour-preserving refactor such as the owner probe above
flags.why: The greps match specific names and strings; a refactor that keeps those names still passes.

flags.claim: The same '-' value also keeps the startup loop waiting while org.bluez is actually owned; ... was only reproduced with a stubbed busctl
flags.why: Not in my evidence. Consistent with code: line 20 rejects '-', and busctl prints '-' for an owned name when credentials or the PID are missing (busctl.c 330-333, 339-349 with ersatz dash at 259). I did not reproduce a persistent '-' for an owned name and did not run that stub. The draft's conditional qualifier is appropriate.

flags.claim: SIGTERM to the whole process group (the default KillMode=control-group) stopped it in 1 to 3 ms ...; using sleep "$poll_interval" & wait $! avoids the delay
flags.why: The 1-3 ms figure is correct for a process-group SIGTERM used as a stand-in for control-group mode (s12), not a systemd run. The sleep & wait variant was not run by me; standard bash semantics support it.

flags.claim: GetNameOwner ... fails with `no such name` when it is absent
flags.why: The message text came from the reference dbus-daemon in the sandbox; dbus-broker (production) text was not checked. An implementation should key off the exit status or error name, not the message.

flags.claim: the old unit left the agent alive and registered with a daemon that no longer existed
flags.why: Nit. The test ran the old unit's ExecStart command (bt-agent -c NoInputNoOutput) directly, without systemd. Behaviour under systemd is the same because Restart=on-failure cannot act while the process is alive.

flags.claim: Adding another name that sorts before org.bluez, with its own changing PID, would catch that.
flags.why: Verified for this check. A mock row printed before org.bluez catches the filterless awk mutant whether its PID changes or stays stable, and the real supervisor passes. The mock prints rows in its own order, so 'printed before' is the relevant property, not sorting. Flagged as a wording nit only.

flags.claim: test/cli fails on current quattro at an unrelated environment-dependent assertion before its metadata check
flags.why: Nit. The failure was observed in the review sandbox (identical on tip and merged), not established for quattro generally; the draft already says environment-dependent.
Outside my evidence; the coordinator verifies models and efforts.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the supervisor fixes the stale-agent problem from #11936. With the real bluez-tools `bt-agent` against a fake BlueZ on a private bus, running the old unit's `ExecStart` command left the agent alive and registered with a daemon that no longer existed. The new daemon had no agent. Under the supervisor, the replacement was detected and the stale agent killed, and the restarted agent registered with the live daemon. The findings below concern cost, robustness and rollout; none stopped the fix from working in the tested scope. The main suggestion is to probe only the `org.bluez` owner instead of listing the whole bus. That also removes one cause of the second finding below.

```text
old unit     bluetoothd B1 ──replaced──▶ B2
             bt-agent registered with B1, still running ──▶ B2 has 0 agents

this PR      poll sees org.bluez PID change ──▶ supervisor exits 1, kills bt-agent
             (measured ~2 s after replacement at the default 2 s poll)
             restart ──▶ new bt-agent registered with B2
             (~2.9 s after B2 appeared, with RestartSec=1 simulated)
```

**Verified** in the same setup:
- BlueZ stopping with no replacement is also handled. The restarted supervisor waits and registers once BlueZ returns.
- The startup wait does not D-Bus-activate `org.bluez`.
- `bt-agent` does ignore SIGTERM (bluez-tools `src/bt-agent.c` wires SIGTERM to the SIGUSR1 handler), and the trap's SIGKILL cleans it up on stop.
- `bluetooth-agent-test.sh` passes on the head and on the head merged onto current `quattro`, fails on the merge base, and caught four behavioural mutants.

### Every session lists the entire system bus every 2 seconds

`bluez_pid()` runs `busctl --system list`, which lists every unique, well-known and activatable name and queries credentials for each owned name. On a private test bus with 124 names, one call made 188 D-Bus method calls and took about 10 ms. `busctl --system call … GetNameOwner s org.bluez` made 2 calls and took about 1.5 ms. The loop runs for the whole session in every logged-in user's manager, spawning `busctl`, `awk` and `sleep` each time.

The removed `ExecCondition` used to skip the unit when `bluetooth.service` was inactive. Now, on a machine where `/sys/class/bluetooth` exists but BlueZ is disabled or never starts, the unit stays `active (running)` and polls indefinitely with no agent.

**Impact:** a small but permanent background cost on every session where the unit runs, including machines with a Bluetooth adapter that never run BlueZ. The real system-bus size and dbus-broker timings were not measured; the call count scales with the number of names on the bus.

**Suggested change:** query only the `org.bluez` owner and compare its unique name (for example `:1.2`), which is never reused on a bus. On the test bus (reference `dbus-daemon`), `GetNameOwner` returned `s ":1.2"` when BlueZ was present, failed with `no such name` when it was absent, and did not activate the name in either case. dbus-broker's error text was not checked. An event-driven `NameOwnerChanged` watch would remove polling entirely (not tested here).

### A failed probe is treated as a BlueZ replacement

```bash
current_bluez_pid=$(bluez_pid)
if [[ $current_bluez_pid != "$initial_bluez_pid" ]]; then   # "" or "-" also differs
  stop_agent
  exit 1
```

Any empty or `-` result is compared as a new owner. That includes a `busctl` error, or a row whose PID credential lookup failed (`busctl` prints `-` in that case). With a `busctl` wrapper that failed once while the owner never changed, the supervisor exited 1 and killed the working agent. The same `-` value also keeps the startup loop waiting while `org.bluez` is actually owned.

**Impact:** a transient probe failure causes an unnecessary restart with no agent registered for about 1 second. The persistent `-` case is conditional on BlueZ's PID credential being unavailable and was only reproduced with a stubbed `busctl`.

**Suggested change:** exit only when the probe succeeds with a different owner, or definitively reports the name absent. Treat other errors as "unknown, poll again". Comparing unique names as suggested above removes the dependence on the PID column, but a failed call still needs this handling.

### Running sessions keep the old agent until the next login

The PR adds no migration. Arch's user daemon-reload hook reloads unit files after the package update but does not restart running units. So an already-running `bt-agent.service` keeps the old `ExecStart=/usr/bin/bt-agent` process and stays stale across a later BlueZ restart in that session. Sessions where the old `ExecCondition` skipped the unit stay inactive until the next login.

**Impact:** on existing sessions, the fix only takes effect after the next login. Until then a BlueZ restart can still leave pairing without an agent.

**Suggested change (optional):** add a migration that restarts the unit for existing sessions without enabling units the user disabled. `systemctl --user try-restart bt-agent.service` covers running units. Sessions the old `ExecCondition` skipped would also need a restart when the unit is enabled. `migrations/1789130779.sh` and `migrations/1785608166.sh` restart user units in a similar way.

**Optional:** `KillMode=mixed` sends SIGTERM only to the supervisor. bash runs the TERM trap only after the foreground `sleep` finishes, so stops took up to about 2 s. SIGTERM to the whole process group, standing in for the default `KillMode=control-group` (not run under systemd), stopped it in 1 to 3 ms with the agent killed. Either dropping `KillMode=mixed` or using `sleep "$poll_interval" & wait $!` avoids the delay. `TimeoutStopSec=3` already bounds it.

**Optional test improvement:**
- The `busctl` mock prints only an `org.bluez` row. A supervisor that drops the `$1 == "org.bluez"` filter from the `awk` still passes both cases. A mock that also prints another name before `org.bluez`, with its own PID, catches that mutant while the real supervisor still passes.
- The new `systemd-test.sh` greps supervisor implementation strings (`while :`, `initial_bluez_pid=$(bluez_pid)`, `sleep "$poll_interval"`, the comparison expression). They add nothing over the behavioural test and can fail on a behaviour-preserving refactor such as the owner probe above.

**Related open PRs:** these change the same `bt-agent.service` lines and conflict with this one:
- #13258 and #9131 address the same login race differently.
- #8929 feeds `bt-agent` stdin through `yes`.
- #12897 and #9965 replace `bt-agent` with a new `omarchy-bluetooth-agent`.

The owner supervision here still applies if `bt-agent` stays (#13258, #9131, #8929). #12897's agent registers from an `org.bluez` name watch, so going by its source it already re-registers on its own (not run).

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the head `46b62ae` against the merge base and current `quattro`, plus bluez-tools (the commit Arch packages), BlueZ 5.87 and systemd v262 source. The runtime tests used the real `bt-agent`, a fake BlueZ on a private reference `dbus-daemon` (not dbus-broker), and a simulated restart delay. There was no real systemd user manager, `bluetoothd`, adapter or pairing, and no hardware test. In the test sandbox, `test/cli` fails on current `quattro` at an unrelated environment-dependent assertion before its metadata check, so that check was replicated separately and passes.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
